name: Biotechnology
one_liner: Biotechs develop biologic and novel-modality therapies, typically burning cash for years on binary clinical bets funded by equity markets and pharma partnerships.
how_it_makes_money: Most biotechs have no product revenue and fund themselves with venture capital, public equity and partnership payments (upfronts, milestones, royalties). Successful ones sell approved therapies at high prices, or are acquired by larger pharma companies.
revenue_formula: Partnership revenue = upfront payment + milestones × probability of reaching them + royalty rate × partner sales
Product revenue = eligible patients × treatment rate × share × net price per patient
Asset value (rNPV) = Σ probability-weighted future cash flows discounted - remaining development cost
cost_structure: R&D: clinical trials and research, the bulk of spend for pre-revenue biotechs
Manufacturing: complex biologics and cell/gene therapy production, often outsourced
General and administrative: IP, legal, public-company costs
Commercial build-out: launch and sales infrastructure if going it alone
margins: Most biotechs are unprofitable and measured by cash runway; the few commercial-stage leaders earn pharma-like margins, with outcomes driven by clinical success and pricing.

key_metrics.name: Cash runway
key_metrics.what: Months of operation funded by current cash; determines financing timing and dilution risk.

key_metrics.name: Burn rate
key_metrics.what: Net cash spent per period; the key operating discipline for pre-revenue firms.

key_metrics.name: Probability of success by phase
key_metrics.what: Odds of advancing through each trial phase; historically low overall from Phase I.

key_metrics.name: Risk-adjusted NPV (rNPV)
key_metrics.what: Probability-weighted value of the pipeline; underpins deals and valuations.

key_metrics.name: Enterprise value vs. cash
key_metrics.what: How much the market values the pipeline beyond cash; signals investor sentiment.

key_metrics.name: Deal terms (upfront, milestones, royalties)
key_metrics.what: Economics of licensing deals; shows how value is shared with partners.

trends: Funding environment tightening and reopening in cycles, forcing pipeline prioritization
Big pharma acquiring biotechs to refill pipelines ahead of patent cliffs
Growth of new modalities such as cell and gene therapy, ADCs and RNA medicines
China-based biotechs emerging as a major source of licensed assets
AI-enabled drug discovery platforms attracting capital
FDA staffing and policy changes creating regulatory uncertainty

case_angles.question: A biotech has one Phase II asset and 18 months of cash. Should it partner, raise, or sell?
Should a biotech commercialize its first approved drug itself or license it to pharma?
How should a gene therapy with a one-time cure be priced?
Should a biotech with a platform technology enter a new therapeutic area?

interview_hooks: How should society pay for one-time, very high-priced cures?
Does AI meaningfully raise the odds of clinical success, or mainly speed discovery?
Is the rise of China-origin assets a threat or an opportunity for US biotech?
